title: Custom software development for businesses
description: Custom software for small and growing businesses anywhere: web apps, internal tools, inventory systems, CRMs and automations, designed and built by one developer.
intro: If your team runs part of the business on spreadsheets, WhatsApp threads and copy-and-paste, that work can usually become software. I design and build custom web applications for businesses in India and abroad, and look after them after launch.
facts: Web apps, internal tools, ERPs, CRMs and automations
React, Next.js and cloud hosting on AWS
India, Saudi Arabia, Poland and Nepal
The code, the data and every account

sections.title: What custom software is, in plain terms
body: Custom software is built around the way your business already works, instead of changing the business to fit a product. It runs in the browser, so your team opens it on a laptop or a phone with nothing to install, and only the people you allow can sign in.

It makes sense when ready-made tools almost fit but leave gaps that people fill by hand, when the same information is typed into three places, or when a large platform costs more every year than building exactly what you use.

items.title: Internal tools and dashboards
items.text: One screen that shows the numbers and tasks your team checks every morning, instead of five spreadsheets.

items.title: Inventory and catalogue systems
items.text: Products, codes, prices and photos in one library, with catalogues you can share in a click.

items.title: CRMs, quotations and invoices
items.text: Every customer and conversation in one place, and documents generated from the data instead of retyped.

items.title: Customer portals and bookings
items.text: Places where your customers sign in to place orders, track work, upload documents or book a time.

items.title: Automations and integrations
items.text: Email, PDFs, payment gateways and the tools you already use, connected so the repetitive steps happen on their own.

items.title: AI features
items.text: Drafting, summaries and search built into the tool, with a person checking what matters.

sections.title: Software already in daily use
body: The inventory software I built keeps a whole product library in one place and turns it into catalogues, quotations and pro forma invoices in a few clicks, with a log of every change. Mailwright sends personalised bulk email: write once with fields such as a name or company, import a contact list, and every recipient gets their own version.

steps.title: Map the work as it happens today
steps.text: Who does what, in which tool, and where time is lost or mistakes creep in.

steps.title: Agree the first version in writing
steps.text: The smallest version that removes the most manual work, with screens, features and a timeline.

steps.title: Build in short rounds
steps.text: You use each round on a live preview link and say what to change, so nothing is a surprise at the end.

steps.title: Launch, train and improve
steps.text: Your data is moved across, your team is shown how it works, and the next improvements are planned from real use.

sections.title: What you should own at the end

items.title: The code
items.text: In a repository in your name, so any developer can work on it later.

items.title: The data
items.text: In your own database, exportable whenever you want it.

items.title: The accounts
items.text: Hosting, domain and any paid services registered to your business, not to the developer.

items.title: The documentation
items.text: A plain description of how the system works and how to run it.

faqs.q: How much does custom software cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope: the number of screens, the user roles, the integrations and how much data has to move from your current tools. Every project gets a written quote and timeline before work starts, and the first version is kept small so you see the benefit early.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build?
faqs.a: Timelines are agreed in writing before work starts. A focused first version is usually a matter of weeks; larger systems are built in stages, each one usable on its own.

faqs.q: Can it work with the tools we already use?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Data can be imported from spreadsheets and existing systems, and the software can send email, create PDFs and connect to any service that offers an API.

faqs.q: Is our data safe?
faqs.a: Everyone signs in, each person sees only what their role allows, the data is stored with established cloud providers and backed up, and you can export it at any time.

faqs.q: Do you maintain the software after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Fixes, updates and new features come from the same person who built it, quoted as small projects when you need them.

faqs.q: Do you work with businesses outside India?
faqs.a: Yes. Projects run remotely over email, WhatsApp and video calls with a live preview link. Clients so far are in India, Saudi Arabia, Poland and Nepal.

cta: Describe the work your team does by hand today, and you will get a written plan for the software that can take it over.

title: Custom ERP and CRM software
description: Custom ERP and CRM software for manufacturers, exporters and growing businesses: inventory, catalogues, quotations, pro forma invoices, customers and activity logs in one place.
intro: An ERP keeps your products, stock and paperwork in one place; a CRM keeps your customers and conversations in one place. I build both around the way your business already works, starting with the part that costs your team the most time.
facts: Manufacturers, exporters, traders and service firms
Any browser, with logins and roles

sections.title: Why build your own instead of buying one
body: Large ERP and CRM products are designed for every business at once. Smaller companies end up paying for modules they never open, and still keep spreadsheets for the steps that do not fit.
A custom system contains only what you use, speaks your terms, prints your document formats, and grows one module at a time as the business needs it.

items.text: Codes, categories, materials, prices, photos and specifications, searchable in a second.

items.title: Catalogues
items.text: A selection of products shared as a link or a PDF, with a record of when it was opened.

items.title: Quotations and pro forma invoices

items.title: Customers and enquiries
items.text: Every buyer, every conversation and the next follow-up date, so no enquiry goes cold.

items.title: Orders and production status

items.title: Activity log

sections.title: Built from inside an export business
body: Before building software for manufacturers, I worked as a merchandiser at an export manufacturer: product development, production schedules, and coordinating international buyers and vendors. The inventory software I built since covers exactly that work, with one product library, catalogues, quotations and pro formas in a few clicks, and a log of every change.

steps.title: List what you track and where
steps.text: Products, prices, customers and documents, and the spreadsheets or tools they live in today.

steps.title: Import, do not retype

steps.text: For a short period the new system runs next to the old way, until the team trusts it.

steps.title: Add the next module
steps.text: Once the first part is in daily use, the next one is planned from what the team actually needs.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an ERP and a CRM?
faqs.a: An ERP (enterprise resource planning) system manages the inside of the business: products, stock, orders and documents. A CRM (customer relationship management) system manages the outside: customers, enquiries, conversations and follow-ups. A custom build can do both in one place.

faqs.q: Can you import our existing Excel sheets?
faqs.a: Yes. Product lists, price lists and customer lists can be imported, so nobody retypes them.

faqs.q: Can it make quotations and invoices in our format?
faqs.a: Yes. Your layout, logo, terms, currencies and units, generated from the data in the system.

faqs.q: Can our team use it on a phone?
faqs.a: Yes. It runs in the browser and works on phones, tablets and laptops, with each person seeing only what their role allows.

faqs.q: Who owns the system?
faqs.a: You do: the code, the database and the hosting account are in your name.

cta: Tell me which spreadsheets your team lives in, and you will get a written plan for the system that replaces them.

sections.title: Experience
body: As a UI/UX developer at TechBuzz Ideas I designed interfaces for websites, custom software and mobile apps, and I now lead delivery of client web and software projects there as project manager. My own experiments include a camera-based live translator and several AI tools.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build an app?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of screens, features and integrations. You get a written scope and timeline before work starts, and a first version focused on one core job comes much sooner than a full product.

faqs.q: Do I need both iOS and Android?
faqs.a: Usually yes, because your customers use both. Building both from one codebase is often the sensible choice, and the right approach is decided per project.

faqs.q: Whose account is the app published under?
faqs.a: Yours. The app goes out under your own Apple and Google developer accounts. Apple charges a yearly developer fee and Google a one-time fee, paid to them directly.

faqs.q: Can you turn my website into an app?
faqs.a: Yes, but first check whether you need to: a well-built website can be added to the home screen and work much like an app. If you need native features, the app can share content and data with the website.

faqs.q: Do you maintain the app after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Operating system updates, fixes and new features, from the person who built it.

cta: Tell me what the app has to let people do, and you will get an honest answer on app or website, and a written plan.

faqs.q: Will AI replace my staff?
faqs.a: In a small business it mostly removes the repetitive part of their work: first drafts, summaries and sorting. People keep the judgement, the relationships and the final say.

faqs.q: Which AI model do you use?
faqs.a: Whichever suits the task and the budget, from providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic or Google. The integration is built so the model can be changed later.

faqs.q: Can an assistant answer from our own documents?
faqs.a: Yes. It can be given your FAQs, product data, policies and documents, answer from them, and point to where the answer came from.

faqs.q: What does it cost to run?
faqs.a: AI providers charge per use, so running costs depend on volume. You get an estimate before anything is built, and usage limits can be set.

faqs.q: Can you also make my business show up in ChatGPT and Google AI answers?
faqs.a: Yes, that is generative engine optimization: making your website easy for AI assistants to read, trust and cite.

cta: Tell me which task eats your team's time, and you will get an honest view of whether AI can do it, and a written plan if it can.

steps.text: If a tool removes most of them, buy it. If the marks stay, custom software will usually pay for itself.

sections.title: The middle path
body: Most businesses do not need to replace everything. Keep standard tools for standard jobs such as accounting and email, and build a small custom system for the part that is unique to you, connected to the tools you already use.

sections.title: A real example
body: Export manufacturers often run their product library in spreadsheets and build every catalogue and quotation by hand, because general inventory tools do not fit how they sell. The inventory software I built does that one job: a single product library that turns into catalogues, quotations and pro formas in a few clicks.

faqs.q: Is custom software expensive?
faqs.a: It costs more upfront and often less over time, because there are no per-user subscriptions and no paying for features you do not use. A small first version keeps the starting cost down.

faqs.q: What if the developer disappears?
faqs.a: That is why the code, the data and the accounts must be in your name, with documentation. Then any developer can continue the work.

faqs.q: Can custom software connect to tools we already use?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, through imports, exports and the APIs most modern tools provide.

faqs.q: How do I know if my process is standard?
faqs.a: If a well-known tool covers it without workarounds, it is standard. If your team keeps side spreadsheets next to the tool, it is not.

cta: Describe the process that frustrates your team most, and you will get an honest answer on whether to buy or build.
